caption: Figure 3. VLP approximation for nonlinear operations, exp here, with a floating-point input 𝑖, represented as S-M-E, denoting the sign, mantissa and exponent. More details are in Section 3.1.
subject: how a floating-point LUT lookup for exp() is split into row (mantissa) and element (exponent) temporal subscriptions

groups.why_chosen: Computing exp() from a LUT is split into two temporal subscriptions: the mantissa selects which row of consecutive values to fetch (shared across inputs needing that row), and the exponent then picks the value from that row.
groups.what_to_learn: building a two-step (row, then element) addressing scheme across several small panels before showing the circuit that implements it; pairing a circuit/dataflow panel with an adjacent cycle-by-cycle timing diagram, linked by dashed zoom-callout lines; colour-coded rows/lanes so a shared resource (one LUT row) can be traced to every input that reuses it
